text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A delegation from the German foreign ministry said that Latvia still has a long way to go before visa regulations between the two countries are abolished.
- The former Minister of Finance, Aivars Kreituss, and former parliament speaker, Ilga Kreituse, have decided to set up a new political party, the Labour Party, before the end of the year.

- The council of the Latvian Christian Democratic Union has decided to invite Prime Minister Andris Shkele to take part in the council's next session to discuss its conditions for remaining in the government coalition. The party is a junior member of the six-party government.

- Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said that the final decision about NATO extension eastwards is still not taken and that Latvia must not renounce its strategic goal of becoming a NATO member.
- On November 7 the state budget deficit amounted to 30 million lats.
- Today President Guntis Ulmanis is leaving for an official visit to the U.K. He will stay there until November 15.
